semantic_model: chinook_legacy model.v1 (reproduces all 48 recorded physical queries exactly)

failures.question: Which billing country generated the most revenue?
failures.evidence: The model exposes 33 country spellings where the clean data has 24: 'USA' and 'U.S.A.' stay separate. A correct query over the model returns 420.07 against gold's 523.06.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT billing_country, ROUND(SUM(total_amount), 2) AS revenue FROM billing GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY revenue DESC, billing_country ASC LIMIT 1

failures.question: How many customers are based in the USA?
failures.evidence: customer.country_code carries four US spellings (U.S.A., US, USA, usa). A correct query over the model counts 5 customers against gold's 13. Stratum also bound the literal 'USA' to billing_country rather than the customer's country.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM customer WHERE country_code IN ('US', 'USA')

failures.question: How many invoices were issued per billing country?
failures.evidence: Same unmerged country spellings: 33 groups against 24.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT billing_country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM billing GROUP BY billing_country ORDER BY billing_country

failures.question: Which artists have no albums in the catalog?
failures.evidence: The model's logical SQL was a valid anti-join. The compiler pushed `album.id IS NULL` into the left join's right-hand side, so every artist looked album-less: 275 rows against 71. The equivalent NOT EXISTS passes.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT artist.name FROM artist WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM album WHERE album.artist_id = artist.id) ORDER BY artist.name

failures.question: Who are the top 10 customers by total amount spent? Give first and last name and the amount.
failures.evidence: Returns exactly the same ten customers as gold. They differ only in the order of customers with tied totals (Barnett and Zimmermann, 43.62), under an order-sensitive scorer. Passes when order is ignored.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, ROUND(SUM(b.total_amount), 2) AS spend FROM customer c JOIN billing b ON c.id = b.customer_number GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY spend DESC, c.last_name ASC LIMIT 10

failures.question: Who are our top customers?
failures.evidence: Same as c-006: the same ten customers, tied totals in a different order.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, ROUND(SUM(b.total_amount), 2) AS spend FROM customer c JOIN billing b ON c.id = b.customer_number GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY spend DESC, c.last_name ASC LIMIT 10

failures.question: Which city has the most customers?
failures.evidence: At least five cities tie at two customers (Berlin, London, Mountain View, Paris, Prague). Gold picks Berlin by alphabetical tie-break; the question has no unique answer.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT UPPER(city) AS city, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customer GROUP BY UPPER(city) ORDER BY n DESC, city ASC LIMIT 1

failures.question: How many tracks have no composer recorded?
failures.evidence: The legacifier replaced the real composer of 74 tracks with a blank or marker (clean data has 'AC/DC', 'Billy Cobham', ...). Stratum counts 1,051 blank composers; gold's 977 cannot be recovered from the legacy data by any system.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM product WHERE composer IS NULL

failures.question: How many albums does Led Zeppelin have?
failures.evidence: 'Led Zeppelin' was not bound to artist.name and `artist` was not linked, so the model matched the album title instead.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM album JOIN artist ON album.artist_id = artist.id WHERE artist.name = 'Led Zeppelin'

failures.question: Show me recent sales.
failures.evidence: Noise entities (playlist_track, product, album) led to a line-level join: 200 rows against 80. With billing alone the 80 rows, dates and totals match gold; only the ordering (descending against gold's ascending) differs.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT order_date_text AS invoice_date, ROUND(total_amount, 2) AS total FROM billing WHERE SUBSTR(order_date_text, 1, 4) = '2025' ORDER BY order_date_text, total_amount

failures.question: What are the top 5 artists by revenue?
failures.evidence: The right entities were linked in the original run. The model sums per-order header totals across order lines, which multiplies revenue. Wrong in 2 of 4 attempts with the right entities.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT artist.name, ROUND(SUM(sol.unit_price * sol.quantity), 2) AS revenue FROM sales_order_line sol JOIN billing b ON b.store_code = sol.store_code AND b.order_number = sol.order_number JOIN product p ON p.id = sol.product_id JOIN album ON album.id = p.album_id JOIN artist ON artist.id = album.artist_id GROUP BY artist.id, artist.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, artist.name ASC LIMIT 5

samples.sql: SELECT a.id, a.name, SUM(b.order_total) AS revenue FROM ( SELECT store_code, order_number, SUM(total_amount) AS order_total FROM billing GROUP BY store_code, order_number ) b JOIN sales_order_line sol ON sol.store_code = b.store_code AND sol.order_number = b.order_number JOIN product p ON p.id = sol.product_id JOIN album al ON al.id = p.album_id JOIN artist a ON a.id = al.artist_id GROUP BY a.id, a.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

SELECT artist.id, artist.name, SUM(sales_order_line.quantity * sales_order_line.unit_price) AS revenue FROM product JOIN sales_order_line ON product.id = sales_order_line.product_id JOIN album ON product.album_id = album.id JOIN billing ON sales_order_line.order_number = billing.order_number AND sales_order_line.store_code = billing.store_code JOIN artist ON album.artist_id = artist.id GROUP BY artist.id, artist.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

SELECT artist.name AS artist_name, SUM(sales_order_line.quantity * sales_order_line.unit_price) AS revenue FROM product JOIN sales_order_line ON product.id = sales_order_line.product_id JOIN album ON product.album_id = album.id JOIN billing ON sales_order_line.order_number = billing.order_number AND sales_order_line.store_code = billing.store_code JOIN artist ON album.artist_id = artist.id GROUP BY artist.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

failures.question: What is the average number of line items per invoice?
failures.evidence: The right entities were linked. The model groups by order_number without store_code, though order numbers restart per store (a composite key). Wrong in every valid attempt.

counterfactual_correct_query.logical_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT b.store_code || '-' || b.order_number), 3) AS avg_lines FROM sales_order_line sol JOIN billing b ON b.store_code = sol.store_code AND b.order_number = sol.order_number
